name: deno
description: A modern runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript.
readmeHtml:
Deno

Deno (/ˈdiːnoʊ/, pronounced dee-no) is a JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly runtime with secure defaults and a great developer experience. It's built on V8, Rust, and Tokio.

Learn more about the Deno runtime in the documentation.

Installation

Install the Deno runtime on your system using one of the commands below. Note that there are a number of ways to install Deno - a comprehensive list of installation options can be found here.

Shell (Mac, Linux):

curl -fsSL https://deno.land/install.sh | sh

PowerShell (Windows):

irm https://deno.land/install.ps1 | iex

Homebrew (Mac):

brew install deno

Chocolatey (Windows):

choco install deno

WinGet (Windows):

winget install --id=DenoLand.Deno

Scoop (Windows):

scoop install main/deno

Build and install from source

Complete instructions for building Deno from source can be found here.

Your first Deno program

Deno can be used for many different applications, but is most commonly used to build web servers. Create a file called server.ts and include the following TypeScript code:

Deno.serve((_req: Request) => {
  return new Response("Hello, world!");
});

Run your server with the following command:

deno run --allow-net server.ts

This should start a local web server on http://localhost:8000.

Learn more about writing and running Deno programs in the docs.

Additional resources

  • Deno Docs: official guides and reference docs for the Deno runtime, Deno Deploy, and beyond.
  • Deno Standard Library: officially supported common utilities for Deno programs.
  • JSR: The open-source package registry for modern JavaScript and TypeScript
  • Developer Blog: Product updates, tutorials, and more from the Deno team.

Contributing

We appreciate your help! To contribute, please read our contributing instructions.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A secure, modern JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly runtime built natively on V8, Rust, and Tokio.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Deno securely executes JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly in a restrictive sandbox by default, requiring explicit permission from the user to access files, networks, or system environments. Built fundamentally upon the V8 JavaScript engine, Rust, and the Tokio event loop, it prioritizes ironclad security and an exceptional out-of-the-box developer experience. The runtime includes an integrated suite of essential tooling, providing a built-in formatter, linter, test runner, and dependency inspector without ever relying on external toolchains or heavy configuration files. By fully adhering to modern web-standard APIs, it allows developers to write isomorphic code seamlessly.
keyFeatures: Secure Execution: Blocks file, network, and environment access entirely out of the box unless explicitly permitted via command-line flags.
Native TypeScript Support: Compiles and executes TypeScript directly without requiring tsc, Babel, or complex external transpilation pipelines.
Integrated Tooling: Bundles essential development tools including a highly opinionated formatter, linter, and fast test runner into a single executable.
Web API Adherence: Implements standard web APIs like fetch and WebSockets strictly, instead of relying on legacy custom Node.js counterparts.
High Performance Foundation: Leverages Rust, the V8 engine, and Tokio for deeply memory-safe and highly efficient asynchronous execution.

useCases.title: Secure Server Deployment
useCases.description: Companies deploy untrusted or third-party backend code safely by aggressively restricting its network and filesystem access via the permission model.

useCases.title: Zero-Config TypeScript Development
useCases.description: Teams immediately start building server-side applications in TypeScript without wasting hours configuring Webpack, Babel, or tsconfig files.

useCases.title: Isomorphic Application Building
useCases.description: Engineers write business logic once and run it interchangeably across browser and server environments using standardized fetch APIs.

useCases.title: Streamlined Toolchain Operations
useCases.description: Projects eliminate heavy node_modules folders and complex build scripts by relying entirely on Deno's fast built-in formatting and testing tools.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Backend developers and TypeScript engineers seeking a secure, highly integrated, and modern alternative to Node.js for modern web services.
